notes: Two passes, both HOLDS, and the second confirmed a self-correction that changes what this PR's headline result means. PASS 1 attacked the gate's ability to report success while verifying nothing -- the failure this repo has shipped six times and the one that would matter most here. It confirmed the gate reports '0 of N' and never 'verified' on all-false, empty, missing and malformed records; that sanitiser-version drift is UNCOMPARABLE, neither passed nor failed; that the recursion guard fires on every argv form tried, including absolute paths, a --pr form and a different working directory, since detection is by basename and cwd is forced to the repo root; that an exit mismatch fails before the digest is even compared; and that a deleted script or missing interpreter produces a loud FAIL rather than a swallowed exception. It independently reproduced the HANDOFF.md 2214-versus-2262 discrepancy and confirmed the PR's own diagnosis of its cause, re-derived the 3-of-101 figure by walking all twelve records, and judged the refusal to back-fill the eleven older records correct -- their digests came from throwaway per-session sanitisers, so a back-filled digest would assert a reproducibility never captured. It found ONE structural thing and one false citation. The structural finding: main() returned 0 whenever failures was empty, so 'nothing checked' and 'everything matched' shared an exit code -- harmless while report-only, load-bearing the moment a blocking PR inherits it, because an author could mark every command unverifiable with a plausible enum reason and take a green gate having re-executed nothing. Nothing validates that a stated reason is TRUE of its command. The citation finding: scripts/lwb_check_proof.py and its test module both cited SPEC-d2-ci-reexecution.md, a session scratchpad file never committed and never to be committed, and lwb_check_state_claims.py already carried the same defect citing an absent SPEC-b -- a second instance, so a convention forming rather than a typo. BETWEEN PASSES, chasing a loose observation in an implementer report found a third thing that neither the reviewer nor the author had caught across a merge and three prior review passes: lwb_handoff.py --check prints HANDOFF.md's byte count, which moves with the generated block's live content, so its digest can NEVER reproduce across commits -- and proof/20.json marked it verifiable: true. The gate's celebrated first mismatch was therefore real but misdiagnosed: the author had attributed it to the regeneration-ordering circularity and written a protocol rule on that reading. The ordering rule stands on its own merits; the reasoning given for it did not. PASS 2, this record, verified all of it: three distinct exit states that cannot read as success, with NOTHING_REEXECUTED printing 'THIS PROVES NOTHING (not success, not a check)'; the enum-honesty hole named un-softened in the plan document rather than papered over; an independently re-run citation sweep finding zero remaining SPEC- references and agreeing that the one external owner document left cited was the right call; the byte counts confirmed by git show at both commits and the determinism confirmed by three identical runs at a fixed checkout; and the other two verifiable commands read at source, each printing a single fixed literal with nothing state-derived. MOST IMPORTANTLY it attacked the record edit itself, because a proof record being modified is where this could go wrong: git diff between the record as merged on main and as corrected here shows exactly one hunk changing verifiable true to false plus an appended unproven entry, with argv, exit, expect_exit, tail and sha256 absent from the diff entirely. Classification corrected, evidence untouched -- the boundary the PR draws, verified rather than asserted. The figure dropped from 3 of 101 to 2 of 101, all matched, and the reviewer agreed a smaller honest number beats a larger one containing a command whose reproducibility was a byte-count coincidence. It also judged the general rule's opening sentence imprecise -- 'invariant at the recorded commit' is not the test, since --reexecute runs at whatever commit is checked out now -- which the author then tightened in both proof/README.md and the recorder docstring, citing PR #20's own mistake as the case that satisfied the weaker wording and still failed. NOT VERIFIED: whether digests reproduce on a real GitHub-hosted runner, which is this PR's stated open experiment and the reason it lands report-only; whether a continue-on-error step's exit code is surfaced differently in the Actions UI; lwb_check_env_leak.py end to end, needing a repository secret no reviewer holds; and whether the external tool-stack-decisions.md is filed where the text says. KNOWN LIMIT: reviewer_was_dispatched_by_author is true -- this reviewer shares the authoring session's token and is a subagent of it. An audit trail, not proof of independent review. REBOUND from 61a980e4af43 to e6215df1545e: after this review cleared, the pr-authority gate from PR #20 was found to forbid the very correction PR #21 exists to make -- it required every record ADDED OR MODIFIED by a PR to declare that PR's number, so correcting proof/20.json was rejected because that record must keep declaring 20. Fixing it (added must declare this PR, modified must keep its own) is a substantive change to scripts/, so the head moved and this record follows it. The reviewer did not examine that fix; it is covered by the next review pass, not this verdict.
